subject: MAP: three-path eval & close timetable — hosting + geo recommendations
body:
----- Message 1/6 -----
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@helixtx.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP draft + quick question on geo/PHI handling

Hi Asha —

Thanks again for the time last week. Attached is a first-pass MAP and evaluation checklist I promised; it lays out a 6–8 week PoC -> pilot plan and the decision gates we typically use for hosting mode.

Quick question to help us recommend the right lanes: for your EU customers, does Helix require data residency (data-at-rest + inference processing) inside EU for all PHI flows, or only for EU-based patients?

High level we see three realistic paths for Helix:
- Hosted API for non-PHI, low-touch, fastest time-to-value
- Dedicated capacity (regional pools) for predictable throughput and segregation of corp customers
- Private (VPC / on-prem) for contracts that require strict residency and additional controls

If you can confirm the EU residency constraint and the expected percent of requests that are PHI, we’ll draft a recommended split (e.g., Dedicated US for dev/eng + Private EU for PHI) and include estimated pricing delta in the MAP.

Attached: MAP-HelixSprint-v2.xlsx (draft)

Best,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
attachments: [MAP-HelixSprint-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

----- End message 1 -----

----- Message 2/6 -----
From: Asha Menon <asha@helixtx.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: MAP draft + quick question on geo/PHI handling

Camila,

Thanks — quick answers:
- Yes, EU data residency is required for PHI for EU patients. Processing must be within EU boundaries (both storage and inference).
- We estimate ~30% of calls will be PHI once integrated with our clinical intake flows; could be higher for EU launches.

We attached the security questionnaire (SOC2 excerpts and some network constraints) — Im putting Procurement on copy for the commercial timeline.

If you can propose a MAP that keeps EU PHI fully within EU (private or dedicated EU nodes) and a costed timeline, we can review internally next week.

Best,
Asha Menon
Head of Platform, Helix Therapeutics
attachments: [SOC2-extract.pdf (doc excerpt)]

----- Message 3/6 (internal) -----
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Helix asks re: EU PHI — recommendation + cost delta

Team —

Asha confirmed EU residency must be enforced for PHI (~30% of calls, could rise). Procurement is in the loop and wants a precise MAP + timeline.

Asks:
1) Recommend default deployment lane (hosted/dedicated/private) for Helix given: US dev + staging, EU PHI required, hybrid traffic.
2) Rough cost delta and expected lead times for private EU onboarding vs dedicated EU pool.
3) Map milestones I can present to their Procurement (SOW/MSA sign, security onboarding, PoC, pilot, go-live).

I sketched a hybrid option in the attached draft but want your short take before I send back.

Attachment I sent them: MAP-HelixSprint-v2.xlsx

Thanks — cami
Camila Reyes

----- End message 3 -----

----- Message 4/6 -----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helix asks re: EU PHI — recommendation + cost delta

Cami —

My recommendation (short):
- US: Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for production; faster to reach their SLA targets and isolates noisy neighbors.
- EU PHI: Private deployment in EU (customer VPC with our private control plane) for full residency, KMS integration, and audit log export. This covers the legal ask.
- Non-PHI EU traffic: route to Dedicated EU (smaller pool) or Hosted if they want lower cost for non-sensitive workloads.

Lead times & cost delta (ballpark):
- Dedicated (EU) provision: 2–3 weeks to provision and validate; marginal monthly delta: ~+30% vs hosted for similar throughput.
- Private (EU) onboarding: 6–8 weeks (security/legal review, network setup, KMS/HSM integration). Setup fee + ~+60% monthly unit cost vs hosted depending on sizing.

Milestones for MAP to present:
1) SOW & MSA signed (Procurement) — Target: 2 weeks after commercial approval
2) Security intake & SOC2 evidence exchange — 1–2 weeks parallel
3) Dedicated EU pool provision + smoke tests — 2–3 weeks
4) Private EU onboarding (if chosen) — 6–8 weeks (can run in parallel with PoC in US)
5) PoC (US, Dedicated) — 2–4 weeks
6) Pilot (EU PHI flows on Private) — 3–6 weeks
7) Go-live & cutover plan — target end of Q1 2027

I attached a cleaned-up MAP sheet with milestone dates. Happy to sync quick if you want to tighten assumptions.

Karthik
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
attachments: [MAP-HelixSprint-v2.xlsx (updated schedule)]

----- End message 4 -----

----- Message 5/6 -----
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@helixtx.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@helixtx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@helixtx.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed MAP + timetable — Helix (Dedicated US / Private EU)

Hi Asha / Tom / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick clarity on residency. Based on the internal recs (Karthiks note below), here is a recommended MAP and timeline wed like to propose:

Summary recommendation:
- Production: Dedicated capacity in US for non-EU and dev workloads; Dedicated EU for non-PHI EU traffic.
- PHI: Private deployment in EU (customer VPC) to satisfy residency + KMS/audit export requirements.

Proposed high-level timetable (target dates):
- Week 0: Commercial approval + MSA countersigned (weve included a sample MSA)
- Wk 1–2: Security intake and evidence exchange (SOC2, network diagram)
- Wk 2–4: Provision Dedicated EU pool + smoke tests
- Wk 2–8: Private EU onboarding (network, KMS, HSM, audit export) — runs in parallel with PoC in US
- Wk 3–6: PoC (US, Dedicated) — sanity and perf tests
- Wk 7–12: Pilot cutover for EU PHI flows to Private environment
- Target go-live: end of Q1 2027 (subject to Procurement signoff)

Cost notes: private EU onboarding is a one-time onboarding fee + monthly premium (we estimate ~+60% relative to hosted per-token at expected volume). Dedicated pools reduce tail latency and give reserved throughput guarantees, with a smaller premium (~+30%). We will provide a line-item cost sheet once you confirm lane selection.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: can you confirm internal purchasing timeline / any PO process?
2) Asha: confirm we can proceed with the parallel path (PoC in US while private EU onboarding starts) — this shortens overall calendar to hit Q1 target.
3) I will open a HubSpot MAP record and send DocuSign for MSA once we have a green light on lane + initial commercial terms. See HubSpot link and DocuSign link below.

Attachments: MAP-HelixSprint-v2.xlsx (schedule), network-segmentation-diagram.png

HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/contacts/8479
DocuSign (sample MSA): https://docusign.example/Envelopes/ABC1234

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
attachments: [MAP-HelixSprint-v2.xlsx, network-segmentation-diagram.png]

----- End message 5 -----

----- Message 6/6 -----
From: Asha Menon <asha@helixtx.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixtx.com>, Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@helixtx.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP + timetable — Helix (Dedicated US / Private EU)

Camila —

This looks sane and addresses our main constraints. Procurement: were aiming to review commercial terms this week; if procurement confirms a standard PO path we can sign MSA and start security exchange immediately.

I approve the parallel path (PoC US while Private EU onboarding starts) — that should help us hit an end-of-Q1 go-live for initial EU customers.

Two small asks before we sign:
1) Please include a short appendix listing the data flows for PHI vs non-PHI and the exact boundaries (inference time processing, logs retention, and telemetry) — well hand that to legal.
2) Procurement: can you send any preferred PO language or supplier forms we should expect?

If Procurement confirms PO cadence, were happy to move forward. Thanks for the clear MAP and timeline — looks lockable.

Best,
Asha
Head of Platform, Helix Therapeutics
